name: Projects & Work Tracking
tagline: Throughput, lead and cycle time, on-time completion, open and blocked work, velocity, logged and billable hours and project budgets for delivery teams
description: Issue and task exports from work-tracking tools (Jira, Azure DevOps Boards, Asana, Monday.com, ClickUp, Trello, Linear, Smartsheet, Wrike, Zoho Projects, Microsoft Project and Planner), timesheet and worklog exports (Harvest, Toggl Track, Clockify, Jira Tempo, Zoho Projects, Keka and Darwinbox PSA) and PMO project-portfolio registers with budget, actual cost, planned and actual dates and RAG status.

fields.label: Issue / task ID
fields.description: Identifies each issue, task or work item; repeats when the file has one row per worklog or sprint.

fields.label: Original estimate (seconds)
fields.description: Jira exports time-tracking fields in seconds.

fields.label: Time spent (seconds)
fields.description: Jira exports time-tracking fields in seconds.

subDomains.name: Issues & tasks
subDomains.description: One row per issue, task or work item with type, status, assignee, priority, created, due and completed dates, and story points or sprint.

subDomains.name: Timesheets & worklogs
subDomains.description: One row per time entry with the person, project, task, date, hours and whether the time is billable.

subDomains.name: Project portfolio
subDomains.description: One row per project with its manager, planned and actual dates, budget, actual cost, % complete and RAG status.

kpis.name: Work items
kpis.definition: Distinct issues, tasks or work items created in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct issue IDs

variants.label: Row count (no issue ID)
variants.caveat: No issue ID column, so every row is counted as one work item. Check the grain.

pitfalls: Jira exports list epics and sub-tasks as rows too; filter by issue type when they should not count as work items.

kpis.name: Completed items
kpis.definition: Work items created in the period that are now done.
kpis.formula: Distinct items with a done status

variants.label: Has a completed date
variants.caveat: No status column, so items with a completed or resolved date count as done.

kpis.name: Done %
kpis.definition: Share of work items created in the period that are done, leaving out cancelled ones.
kpis.formula: Completed items ÷ items not cancelled

variants.label: Done ÷ all items
variants.caveat: No status column, so cancelled items stay in the denominator.

pitfalls: Uses each item's current status, so items created recently always look less done.

kpis.name: Open work items
kpis.definition: Work items created in the period that are not yet done or cancelled.
kpis.formula: Distinct items whose status is not done or cancelled

variants.label: No completed date
variants.caveat: No status column, so items without a completed date count as open.

kpis.name: Issue lead time
kpis.definition: Average days from an item being created to it being done, for completed items.
kpis.formula: Average of (completed date − created date) in days
pitfalls: Open items enter the average only once they are done, so recent periods look faster than they are.
A few very old items skew the average; read the distribution chart next to it.

kpis.name: Sprint velocity
kpis.definition: Average story points completed per sprint.
kpis.formula: Σ story points on done items per sprint, averaged over sprints

variants.label: Points with a completed date per sprint, averaged
variants.caveat: No status column, so items with a completed date count as done.

pitfalls: Velocity is for one team's planning; points are not comparable across teams.
An item carried over several sprints is credited to the sprint named on its row; Jira exports list every sprint it passed through.

kpis.name: Hours logged
kpis.definition: Hours of work logged in the period.
kpis.formula: Σ hours logged

variants.label: Time spent (seconds) ÷ 3,600
variants.caveat: Time spent is read as seconds, as Jira exports it, and converted to hours. Check that the column is in seconds.

kpis.name: Billable hours
kpis.definition: Hours logged that can be billed to a client.
kpis.formula: Σ billable hours (or hours on billable entries)

kpis.name: Billable hours %
kpis.definition: Share of logged hours that are billable.
kpis.formula: Billable hours ÷ hours logged

variants.label: Billable hours ÷ hours, entries with both

pitfalls: This is billable time over time logged, not utilisation over capacity: people who log few hours still look fully billable.

kpis.name: People
kpis.definition: Distinct people assigned work or logging time in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct assignees

kpis.name: Hours per person
kpis.definition: Hours logged per person who logged time in the period.
kpis.formula: Hours logged ÷ people
pitfalls: Part-time staff and people who joined mid-period pull the average down.

kpis.name: Billable amount
kpis.definition: Value of billable time in the period.
kpis.formula: Σ billable amount (or billable hours × billable rate)

variants.label: Billable hours × rate
variants.caveat: No billable amount column, so value is billable hours × billable rate, entry by entry.

variants.label: Hours × rate on billable entries
variants.caveat: No billable amount column, so value is hours × billable rate on billable entries.

kpis.name: Projects
kpis.definition: Distinct projects in the period; on a portfolio register, every listed project.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct projects

kpis.name: Project budget
kpis.definition: Approved budget of the projects in view.
kpis.formula: Σ project budget
pitfalls: A register with one row per project per month repeats the budget on every row; pick a single month before reading totals.

kpis.name: Actual project cost
kpis.definition: Cost incurred on the projects or time entries in view.
kpis.formula: Σ actual cost

kpis.name: Cost overrun %
kpis.definition: How far actual cost runs over (positive) or under (negative) budget, across projects with both figures.
kpis.formula: (Σ actual cost − Σ budget) ÷ Σ budget, projects with both
pitfalls: Projects still running have spent only part of their budget, so the portfolio looks under budget until they finish; compare against earned value where you have it.

kpis.name: Projects at risk %
kpis.definition: Share of projects with a RAG status that are red or amber.
kpis.formula: Red or amber projects ÷ projects with a RAG status

variants.label: Red or amber ÷ projects with a RAG status
Red ÷ projects with a RAG status
variants.caveat: No amber values were recognised, so only red projects count as at risk.

variants.label: Amber ÷ projects with a RAG status
variants.caveat: No red values were recognised, so only amber projects count as at risk.

pitfalls: RAG is a judgement by each project manager; read it next to cost and schedule figures.

kpis.name: On-time completion %
kpis.definition: Share of completed items (tasks or projects) finished on or before their due date.
kpis.formula: Items done by the due date ÷ done items with a due date

variants.label: Done by the due day, per item
Completed on or before the due date, per row
variants.caveat: Compares the full date and time, so an item finished later on its due day counts as late when the due date has no time.

pitfalls: Measured on finished items only, so open items already past their due date are not yet counted late.

kpis.name: Story points completed
kpis.definition: Story points on work items that are done.
kpis.formula: Σ story points on done items

variants.label: Points on items with a completed date
variants.caveat: No status column, so items with a completed date count as done.

kpis.name: Average cycle time
kpis.definition: Average days from work starting on an item to it being done.
kpis.formula: Average of (completed date − start date) in days
pitfalls: Cycle time starts when work starts; lead time starts when the item is created, so it is always the longer of the two.

kpis.name: Bug share
kpis.definition: Share of work items that are bugs or defects.
kpis.formula: Bug items ÷ work items

kpis.name: Blocked items
kpis.definition: Work items whose current status is blocked or on hold.
kpis.formula: Distinct items with a blocked or on-hold status

kpis.name: Items per assignee
kpis.definition: Work items per person assigned work in the period.
kpis.formula: Work items ÷ people
pitfalls: Unassigned items count in the numerator but have no assignee.

kpis.name: Effort overrun %
kpis.definition: How far logged effort runs over (positive) or under (negative) the estimate, on items with both.
kpis.formula: (Σ hours logged − Σ estimated hours) ÷ Σ estimated hours, items with both

variants.label: (Time spent − original estimate) ÷ estimate, in seconds
variants.caveat: Uses Jira's time spent and original estimate, both in seconds; the ratio does not depend on the unit.

pitfalls: Items still in progress have logged only part of their effort, so they pull the figure down until they finish.

kpis.name: Effective billable rate
kpis.definition: Billable amount earned per billable hour.
kpis.formula: Billable amount ÷ billable hours

kpis.name: Cost performance index
kpis.definition: Earned value per unit of actual cost: above 1 is under budget for the work done, below 1 is over.
kpis.formula: Σ earned value ÷ Σ actual cost, projects with both

kpis.name: Schedule performance index
kpis.definition: Earned value per unit of planned value: above 1 is ahead of schedule, below 1 is behind.
kpis.formula: Σ earned value ÷ Σ planned value, projects with both

kpis.name: Budget remaining
kpis.definition: Budget not yet spent, across projects with both a budget and an actual cost.
kpis.formula: Σ budget − Σ actual cost, projects with both

variants.label: Budget − actual cost, projects with both

kpis.name: Average schedule slip
kpis.definition: Average days between the due date and the actual completion, for finished items (negative means early).
kpis.formula: Average of (completed date − due date) in days

kpis.name: Average planned duration
kpis.definition: Average days from planned start to planned end.
kpis.formula: Average of (due or planned end date − start date) in days

kpis.name: Non-billable hours
kpis.definition: Hours logged that cannot be billed: internal work, leave, pre-sales and similar.
kpis.formula: Hours logged − billable hours

kpis.name: Open high-priority items
kpis.definition: Open work items raised at high or critical priority.
kpis.formula: Distinct open items with a high priority

variants.label: High priority, not done or cancelled

kpis.name: Story points (all items)
kpis.definition: Story points on every work item in view, done or not.
kpis.formula: Σ story points

kpis.name: Unassigned items
kpis.definition: Work items with no assignee.
kpis.formula: Distinct items with a blank assignee

kpis.name: Remaining work (hours)
kpis.definition: Hours of work still estimated to remain on the items in view.
kpis.formula: Σ remaining hours

charts.title: Work items created over time
charts.reason: Items created per period are discrete counts, so columns from a zero baseline show incoming demand honestly.

charts.title: Items completed over time
charts.reason: Throughput: items counted in the period they were finished, as columns from zero, to set against the items created.

charts.title: Lead time over time
charts.reason: An average duration recomputed for each completion period, drawn as a line.

charts.title: Hours logged over time
charts.reason: Hours per period are discrete totals, so columns from a zero baseline compare them honestly.

charts.title: Billable hours % over time
charts.reason: A share recomputed for each period from billable and total hours, drawn as a line and never averaged across people.

charts.title: Projects started over time
charts.reason: How the portfolio filled up: projects counted by the period they started, as columns from zero.

charts.title: Work items by status
charts.reason: A few workflow statuses as parts of all items: a donut shows how much is done, in progress or waiting.

charts.title: Work items by type
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across a handful of item types (story, bug, task): a donut shows the mix.

charts.title: Open work by assignee
charts.reason: Who holds the open work: sorted horizontal bars keep names readable. Top 15 plus Others.

charts.title: Work items by epic
charts.reason: Where the work goes: items per epic or parent, sorted, top 10 plus Others.

charts.title: Hours by project
charts.reason: One measure across named projects: sorted horizontal bars, top 10 plus Others.

charts.title: Hours by person
charts.reason: Hours logged per person: sorted bars show who carries the load, top 15 plus Others.

charts.title: Hours by client
charts.reason: Part-to-whole of logged time across a handful of clients: a donut shows the split.

charts.title: Budget vs actual cost by project
charts.reason: Budget and actual cost share one currency axis, so paired bars per project compare them without a second axis.

charts.title: Projects by RAG status
charts.reason: Red, amber and green as parts of the portfolio: a donut shows the health split at a glance.

charts.title: Projects by manager
charts.reason: How the portfolio is spread across project managers: sorted bars, top 12 plus Others.

charts.title: How long items take
charts.reason: Lead times are skewed: a histogram of items per band of days shows the long tail an average hides.

charts.title: Story points completed by sprint
charts.reason: Points completed in each sprint as columns from zero: the run of sprints shows whether velocity is steady enough to plan with.

charts.title: Lead time by priority
charts.reason: Are urgent items really handled faster? Average lead time per priority level, with levels under 20 items hidden.

charts.title: On-time completion by assignee
charts.reason: A rate compared across people: sorted bars of the recomputed on-time share, with people under 15 items hidden.

charts.title: Billable hours % by person
charts.reason: A share compared across people: sorted bars of the recomputed billable %, with people under 10 entries hidden.

charts.title: Hours by weekday
charts.reason: Seven ordered weekdays and one measure: columns show the weekly rhythm and any weekend work.

charts.title: Cost overrun by project
charts.reason: Which projects run over budget: the recomputed overrun % per project, sorted, with under-budget projects below zero.

charts.title: Cost vs schedule performance by project
charts.reason: Two earned-value indices per project: a scatter shows which projects are over budget, behind schedule or both, without a dual axis.

charts.title: Assignee workload
charts.reason: Several measures per person: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

charts.title: Project time summary
charts.reason: Hours, billable hours, billable % and people per project side by side in a sortable table.

charts.title: Project portfolio
charts.reason: Budget, actual cost and overrun per project side by side: the usual PMO portfolio view.

pitfalls: Done %, open items and lead time use each item's current status, so recently created items always look less finished.
Jira exports time-tracking fields (time spent, original estimate) in seconds; Loupe reads them as seconds, so check the unit before trusting hours.
Story points measure one team's own scale; compare velocity within a team over time, never across teams.
A project register with one row per project per month repeats budgets and costs on every row; pick one month before reading totals.
Rates such as done %, on-time completion and billable % are recomputed from counts and hours for every period and group, never averaged across people.
